updatedBySignals.change: Added a response for 'Segment has a no-code audience builder now.'
Rewrote the 'already installed' play: keep Segment for collection, add Hightouch for activation.
Added a question on where AI gets its data, in response to the 'customer AI' messaging shift.

quickDismiss: Segment is great at collecting events. Hightouch activates the customer data you already model in your warehouse, so marketers launch on the full picture without a second copy for the data team to keep in sync.

whereWeWin.point: One source of truth, no second copy
whereWeWin.detail: Audiences are built on the warehouse model the data team already governs. Nothing drifts out of sync, and there's no second profile store to reconcile.
whereWeWin.proof: Whiteboard the data flow: warehouse → Hightouch → destinations, compared with collect → copy → profile store → destinations.

whereWeWin.point: Marketers self-serve on any warehouse data, including events
whereWeWin.detail: Subscriptions, orders, predictions, and support data are all available in the audience builder the day they land in the warehouse.
whereWeWin.proof: Build an audience live using a model the prospect named in discovery, such as LTV, churn score, or subscription tier.

whereWeWin.point: AI Decisioning on the full customer picture
whereWeWin.detail: Agents learn from everything in the warehouse and act through the tools the team already uses.
whereWeWin.proof: Pull the most relevant published Hightouch AI Decisioning case study for the prospect's industry.

whereTheyWin.point: Event collection depth and SDK footprint
whereTheyWin.handle: Agree with it. Position as 'keep Segment for collection, use Hightouch to activate.' That lowers switching risk and avoids a rip-and-replace.

whereTheyWin.point: Already installed, so it feels lower risk
whereTheyWin.handle: Name the risk out loud, then reframe: adding activation on the warehouse is lower risk than copying more data into another platform.
Bring the conversation back to data ownership and to which team maintains the pipelines. Cost questions go to the AE with a TCO worksheet, never ad-hoc numbers.

landmines: When your data team changes a model in the warehouse, how does that change reach your marketing audiences today?
Which customer data lives outside your event stream, like orders, subscriptions, or predictions, and can marketers use it in audiences today?
Where does your AI get its data from: the full warehouse, or a copy of part of it?
Who gets paged when an audience breaks?

objections.objection: "Segment has a no-code audience builder now."
objections.response: "It's a good addition. What is it building on? Ask how those audiences stay in sync when the data team changes the warehouse model, and who fixes it when they don't."

objections.objection: "We already have Segment. Why add another tool?"
objections.response: "Keep it for collection. Hightouch works alongside it and makes everything already in your warehouse usable by marketing, without moving it again."

objections.objection: "Warehouse-native means my data team becomes the bottleneck."
objections.response: "The data team models the data once, and marketers build audiences on it themselves from then on. Let me show you an audience built live without SQL."

objections.objection: "Segment's Reverse ETL does the same thing."
objections.response: "Syncing tables is one piece. Ask about the audience builder, identity resolution, and decisioning on top of that, and test each one in the evaluation."

byPersona.lead: Self-serve audiences on orders, subscriptions, and predictions as well as events. Show a live build.
byPersona.avoid: Architecture talk before they've seen the builder.
byPersona.proofPoint: Demo moment: audience from a prospect-named model in under five minutes.

byPersona.theyCareAbout: Governance, one source of truth, and fewer pipelines to maintain.
byPersona.lead: No second copy and no profile store to reconcile. The warehouse stays the source of truth.
byPersona.avoid: Implying they have to rip out Segment.

byPersona.lead: Product and marketing work from the same models, and AI Decisioning runs experiments continuously.
byPersona.avoid: Overclaiming real-time for in-session use cases. Scope latency needs first.
byPersona.proofPoint: Customer story: experimentation results from a published case study.
